content.user_title: Design Rust Property Tests with Proptest
content.value_statement: Property-based testing can be hard to apply because useful properties and generators are not always obvious. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code propose targeted proptest strategies for Rust code.
actual_capabilities: Suggests roundtrip properties for serialization, encoding, and decoding code.
Identifies invariant checks for sorting algorithms and data structures.
Recommends oracle comparisons against standard library or slower reference implementations.
Shows proptest strategies for domain types with constrained generated values.
Explains shrinking as a way to minimize failing generated cases.
limitations: Focuses on Rust examples that use the proptest crate.
Does not execute tests or verify that generated examples compile.
Requires project-specific knowledge to choose complete domain invariants.
Does not replace deterministic unit tests for known business rules.

use_cases.title: Test Algorithm Implementations
use_cases.description: Create properties for sorting, encoding, parsing, or numeric functions that must behave correctly across many inputs.

use_cases.title: Validate Data Structures
use_cases.description: Define generated operation sequences that check ordering, balance, and consistency after every mutation.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Coverage
use_cases.description: Ask an assistant to suggest missing property tests before merging complex Rust logic.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Properties
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a Rust function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust function and suggest simple proptest properties that should always hold. Focus on edge cases and clear assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Create Roundtrip Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design property-based tests for this Rust roundtrip path. Include suitable input strategies and explain what each property proves.

prompt_templates.title: Test Data Structure Invariants
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest proptest operation sequences for this data structure. Check invariants after each operation and note important generated cases.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Oracle Comparison Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this optimized Rust algorithm against a trusted reference implementation using proptest. Propose strategies, invariants, and failure triage steps.

output_examples.input: A Rust parser accepts names and ages from a comma-separated string.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes properties for no panics, valid generated records, rejected malformed input, and roundtrip formatting checks.

output_examples.input: A custom sort implementation returns reordered integer vectors.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests checking sorted order, preserved length, preserved elements, idempotence, and comparison with the standard sort.

output_examples.input: A B-tree supports insert and remove operations.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends generated operation sequences that verify balance, ordering, lookup behavior, and consistency after each mutation.

best_practices: Start with properties that describe observable behavior, not implementation details.
Use constrained strategies when generated values must satisfy domain rules.
Keep failing cases small and readable so shrinking results are easy to debug.
anti_patterns: Generating only trivial values that never exercise boundary conditions.
Replacing all example-based tests with broad properties that hide specific requirements.
Writing properties that duplicate the same flawed logic as the implementation under test.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps design Rust property-based tests with proptest for algorithms, parsers, data structures, and serialization code.

faq.question: Does it run my tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance and examples, but it does not execute commands or verify compilation.

faq.question: Which Rust testing crate does it target?
faq.answer: It targets proptest and uses proptest concepts such as strategies, generated inputs, invariants, and shrinking.

faq.question: Can it help with parser testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests properties such as no panics, valid input acceptance, malformed input rejection, and roundtrip behavior.

faq.question: Is it useful for data structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends generated operation sequences and invariant checks for stateful structures.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the Rust code, expected behavior, known constraints, and any reference implementation or examples.
